summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

primary_citations.citation_text: Montana - Title 41, Chapter 3 (Child Abuse and Neglect – mandatory reporting and protective services)

regulations_applicable.title: Department 37 - PUBLIC HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed; a youth-in-need-of-care adjudication is not a prerequisite to temporary investigative authority under § 41-3-433 or to a court-ordered treatment plan under § 41-3-443(1) where the parents admit or stipulate to the allegations.
key_cases.relevance: It shows the practical effect of a parent agreeing to the allegations and to services without a contested adjudication.
key_cases.quote: a YINC adjudication is not always required for TIA and court-approved treatment plans

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed: the Department made the reasonable efforts required by § 41-3-423(1) where it prepared and explained a treatment plan and offered services, even though the father never signed or returned the plan and the court approved it on the Department's motion.
key_cases.relevance: It shows that a parent's initial willingness to cooperate does not convert the case into a voluntary one; the plan is imposed by court order once the parent fails to sign.
key_cases.quote: From our review of the record, we conclude the Department provided reasonable efforts as required by § 41-3-423(1), MCA.

search_keywords: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services

state_agency.name: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services, Child and Family Services Division

mandatory_reporters: Physicians, residents, interns, and hospital staff engaged in the admission, examination, care, or treatment of persons — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(a)
Nurses, osteopaths, chiropractors, podiatrists, medical examiners, coroners, dentists, optometrists, and any other health or mental health professionals — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(b)
School teachers, other school officials, and employees who work during regular school hours — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(d)

Social workers licensed pursuant to Title 37, child protection investigators, child reunification specialists, operators or employees of any registered or licensed day-care or substitute care facility, staff of a resource and referral grant program organized under § 52-2-711 or of a child and adult food care program, and operators or employees of a child-care facility — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(e)
Foster care, residential, and institutional workers — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(f)
Peace officers and other law enforcement officials — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(g)
Members of the clergy, subject to the confessional and canon-law exceptions — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(h), (6)(b)–(c)
Guardians ad litem and court-appointed advocates authorized to investigate a report of alleged abuse or neglect — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(i)
Employees of entities that contract with the department to provide direct services to children — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(j)
Department employees while in the conduct of their duties — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2)(k)

Added duty: a professional listed in § 41-3-201(2)(a) or (2)(b) who is involved in the delivery or care of an infant must report any infant known to the professional to be affected by a dangerous drug, as defined in § 50-32-101 — Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(3)
reporting_details: Montana is not a universal-reporter state: only the professionals and officials listed in Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-201(2) must report promptly to the department when, in their professional or official capacity, they know or have reasonable cause to suspect a child is abused or neglected, while § 41-3-201(4) allows any other person to report voluntarily.

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Written safety and risk assessment furnished
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Statute states no penalty; within 60 days the child protection investigator must furnish the written safety and risk assessment to the department and, on request, to the family (Mont. Code Ann. § 41-3-202(6))
